newsitem.title: UK: English wheat sowings up 2.1 pct survey shows.
newsitem.headline: English wheat sowings up 2.1 pct survey shows.

text.p: Autumn and winter wheat sowings in England by December 1996 were up by just 2.1 per cent to 1.845 million hectares, according to the results of the UK farm ministry's December survey, released on Thursday.
Sowings of barley rose by 7.1 per cent compared to a year ago, to 717,000 hectares, the ministry said.
There was an increase of 27.7 per cent to 352,000 hectares in the area of autumn sown oilseed rape, with growers possibly switching from the lower yielding spring crop, the ministry said.

The area of winter beans rose by 1.3 per cent to 67,000 hectares and that of linseed rose by 295.4 pct to 36,000 hectares, although the ministry said that previous year linseed area figures may be unreliable.
Figures for oilseed rape and linseed exclude crops grown on setaside land.
Results for the UK as a whole will be published in April.
The report covers sowings for the 1997 harvest carried out by the survey date.
